title: What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers
titleZh: 如果整个阶层的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么
author: RickJWagner
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Credits Aaron Horwath is the director of AI operations at a creative technology company where he is focused on implementing AI in a way that supports both humans and business.

On a recent morning commute, I sat on a train in one of those awkward four-person configurations with a shared table. Across from me sat a typical commuter: early 30s, slacks, dress shirt, dirty white sneakers, hair a little disheveled, AirPods in, basking in the glow of an open MacBook.

For over half an hour, I listened to this young man as he was on a call explaining, in painfully monotone detail, EBITDAs, margin expansion opportunities, cost structures, ARR, etc. On and on he went until the screeching of the train’s brakes signaled our arrival at the final station. But as everyone else around us began shuffling to disembark, I watched the man begin digging frantically through a leather bag at his side. Intriguing! I wondered what he’d pull out. A copy of “Atomic Habits”? A framed portrait of Gary V? A Mac mini running OpenClaw?

None of the above. Instead, he took out two long knitting needles. Between them dangled a mound of pink yarn. He explained to me that he was making a winter hat for a niece. And for the first time that morning, I noticed a glint of pride and excitement in his eyes.
The hat was a project born from a desire, as he put it, to do something.
summaryZh: Credits Aaron Horwath is the director of AI operations at a creative technology company where he is focused on implementing AI in a way that supports both humans and business.

comments.author: Animats
comments.textRawHtml:
Addressing the question in the title, "What happens if an entire class of workers loses faith in their careers", look at what happened to printers. That was a good skilled trade for centuries. Then it just went away. Phototypesetting took the high volume end. Desktop publishing took the low end. Computer-controlled presses took press operators. And then the newspaper business died.

I've heard homeless former printers talking about the good days at the Burger King near the cable car turntable at Powell and Market. They thought they had careers. Now they're struggling to survive.

Knitting is not the answer. This is a survival issue. Somehow I suspect the author inherited money.
comments.textZhHtml:
解决标题中的问题“如果整个阶级的工人对自己的职业失去信心会发生什么”，看看打印机发生了什么。几个世纪以来，这一直是一项良好的熟练贸易。然后它就消失了。照相排版占据了高产量。桌面出版占据了低端市场。计算机控制的印刷机取代了印刷机操作员。然后报纸生意就消亡了。

我听到无家可归的前印刷商谈论在鲍威尔和市场缆车转盘附近的汉堡王的美好时光。他们以为自己有事业。 现在他们正在为生存而挣扎。

编织不是答案。这是一个生存问题。不知怎的，我怀疑作者继承了钱。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml:
Surprised no one has made the extremely obvious observation that it took literal centuries for printing technology to eliminate the trade of printers, which could not have possibly have employed more than 0.01% of people at its peak.

Compared to the potential obsolescence of 40% to 60% of the US workforce over the course of 10 - 20 years?

You can argue about whether the obsolescence is real or not, but if it is, the plight of the printers is totally incomparable.

Question: What happens when you drive a car at 90 mph into a concrete wall?

Answer: Well, actually just this morning pulling into my parking spot, I bumped into the barrier beneath my tires. It was fine!
children.textZhHtml:
令人惊讶的是，没有人做出极其明显的观察，即印刷技术花了几个世纪的时间才消除了打印机贸易，而打印机在其巅峰时期雇用的人口不可能超过 0.01%。

与 10 - 20 年间美国劳动力 40% 到 60% 的潜在淘汰相比？

你可以争论这种淘汰是真实的还是不是，但是如果是，打印机的困境是完全无法比拟的。

问题：当你以 90 英里/小时的速度驾驶汽车撞上混凝土墙时会发生什么？

答案：嗯，实际上就在今天早上，我把车开进停车位时，就撞到了轮胎下面的护栏上。很好！

children.author: Exoristos
children.textRawHtml:
Most of it actually took about five years, as the manufacturing side of it was outsourced to China and the computer side to India. I was there. Management told us it was "because of 9/11." R.R. Donnelley was one of the world's largest manufacturing companies, a Fortune 50 company -- became a penny stock in a decade or so.

The technologies GP mentions didn't end commercial print -- they were all heavily in use _by_ commercial print.
children.textZhHtml:
其中大部分实际上花了大约五年的时间，因为它的制造部分外包给中国，计算机部分外包给印度。我在那里。管理层告诉我们这是“因为 9/11”。 R.R. Donnelley 是世界上最大的制造公司之一，财富 50 强公司，在十年左右的时间里成为了低价股。

GP 提到的技术并没有结束商业印刷 - 它们都被商业印刷大量使用。

children.author: Exoristos
children.textRawHtml: Oh and the actual driving mechanism was vulture capitalist takeover.
children.textZhHtml: 哦，实际的驱动机制是秃鹫资本主义的接管。

children.author: wongarsu
children.textRawHtml: If printing technology took centuries to eliminate the trade of printers, by the same logic computers took about 80 years to eliminate a large chunk of knowledge workers (and that's just counting until today, we might still be a couple years off)
children.textZhHtml: 如果打印技术花了几个世纪的时间才消除了打印机贸易，那么按照同样的逻辑，计算机花了大约 80 年的时间才消除了一大批知识工作者（这只是到今天为止的计算，我们可能还需要几年时间）

children.author: thegrim33
children.textRawHtml: The difference is that one of those things actually happened, and the other one is your hypothetical extremist/exaggerated/worst possible case of what might happen this time.
children.textZhHtml: 区别在于，其中一件事确实发生了，另一件事是您假设的极端/夸张/最糟糕的情况，这一次可能会发生。

children.author: mbesto
children.textRawHtml:
The entire premise of the article is that we're being promised that an entire workforce is going to be eliminated overnight. The people who are promising this, do not care about what happens to the working class. This is clearly causing anxiety.

The comparison is useful. Printers had decades to pivot and hence the anxiety didn't exist like it does today. Today's capital allocated wants this to happen within a decade.
children.textZhHtml:
这篇文章的整个前提是我们被承诺整个劳动力将在一夜之间被淘汰。做出这一承诺的人并不关心工人阶级会发生什么。这显然会引起焦虑。

这种比较很有用。印刷商有几十年的时间来进行转型，因此焦虑并不像今天那样存在。今天分配的资本希望这在十年内实现。

children.author: senordevnyc
children.textRawHtml: Who are you talking about? Who has promised that the entire workforce is going to be eliminated overnight?
children.textZhHtml: 你在说谁？谁能保证一夜之间全部劳动力被淘汰？

children.author: RobertRies
children.textRawHtml:
And here is a selection of quotes:

-Sam Altman “whole classes of jobs going away”

-Mustafa Suleyman "So white-collar work, where you're sitting down at a computer, either being a lawyer or an accountant or a project manager or a marketing person — most of those tasks will be fully automated by an AI within the next 12 to 18 months."

-Jim Farley “Artificial intelligence is going to replace literally half of all white-collar workers.”

-Dario Amodei predicted that AI could eliminate up to 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs within five years

-Arindam Paul has said that 40-50 percent of white-collar jobs in India could cease to exist because of AI, and an Anthropic researcher had predicted that AI would be able to automate any white-collar job by 2028.
children.textZhHtml:
这里是精选的引言：

-Sam Altman“所有类别的工作都将消失”

-Mustafa Suleyman“白领工作，你坐在电脑前，无论是律师、会计师、项目经理还是营销人员 - 大多数任务将在未来 12 到 18 个月内由人工智能完全自动化。”

-Jim法利“人工智能将取代几乎一半的白领工人。”

-Dario Amodei 预测人工智能可以在五年内消除多达 50% 的入门级白领工作

-Arindam Paul 表示，印度 40-50% 的白领工作可能会因为人工智能而消失，一位人类研究人员预测人工智能将能够通过以下方式实现任何白领工作的自动化： 2028 年。

children.author: foco_tubi
children.textRawHtml: No one is claiming the entire workforce would be eliminated. You’re making that claim up because you misread something along the way.
children.textZhHtml: 没有人声称整个劳动力都会被淘汰。你之所以这么说是因为你一路上误读了一些东西。

children.author: RobertRies
children.textRawHtml: It's genuinely possible English is his second language? It's pretty subtle, but there's a big difference between "an entire" versus "the entire."
children.textZhHtml: 英语真的有可能是他的第二语言吗？这是相当微妙的，但“整体”与“整体”之间有很大的区别。

children.author: smolder
children.textRawHtml: Right. A workforce can contain a workforce, as a set can contain a set.
children.textZhHtml: 正确的。一个劳动力可以包含一个劳动力，就像一个集合可以包含一个集合一样。

children.author: zero-sharp
children.textRawHtml: The parent is making a point about the rate/scale at which technology replaced workers. If you think the hypothetical is too extreme, then what would a more realistic version be? Are you uncertain about the rate of disruption?
children.textZhHtml: 家长强调了技术取代工人的速度/规模。如果你认为这个假设太过极端，那么更现实的版本会是什么呢？您不确定中断的速度吗？

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml: the wise man bowed his head solemnly and spoke: "theres actually zero reason to think about events that haven't happened yet. you imbecile. you fucking moron"
children.textZhHtml: 智者郑重地低下了头，说道：“其实没有理由去思考尚未发生的事情。你这个白痴。你他妈的白痴”

children.author: alsetmusic
children.textRawHtml: I don't think they said that at all. I'm pretty sure they were saying that the thing to think about / discuss is the thing that happened, rather than the hypothetical.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为他们根本没有这么说过。我很确定他们是在说要思考/讨论的事情是已经发生的事情，而不是假设的事情。

children.author: estearum
children.textRawHtml:
My own initial comment literally addressed the uncertainty.

Here:

> You can argue about whether the obsolescence is real or not, but if it is [emphasis in source], the plight of the printers is totally incomparable.

"It hasn't happened yet" is a non-sequitur at best, but obviously the goal of such a "contribution" is to chill discussion. The same "contribution" can be made to any conversation about any possible future events. So long as everyone already knows they're talking about the future, it is not helpful in any way.
children.textZhHtml:
我自己的最初评论确实解决了不确定性。

这里：

>你可以争论过时是否真实，但如果是[强调来源]，打印机的困境是完全无法比拟的。

“它还没有发生”充其量是一个不合逻辑的推论，但显然这种“贡献”的目标是让人们冷静下来讨论。对于任何有关未来可能发生的事件的任何对话都可以做出同样的“贡献”。只要每个人都知道他们正在谈论未来，那就没有任何帮助。

children.author: freejazz
children.textRawHtml: The entire premise of this article is a hypothetical
children.textZhHtml: 本文的整个前提都是假设

children.author: altmanaltman
children.textRawHtml: Yeah + the world was much different than it is today. It trivializes the risk by saying we have seen it before and we were okay when its a fundamentally different problem in many aspects.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，当时的世界与今天有很大不同。它轻视了风险，说我们以前见过这种情况，而且我们没问题，但实际上它在很多方面都是一个根本不同的问题。
